A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Low-Rank Thinning by the same authors. Their main sections and Appendices A–L can be matched, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet attention benchmarks in Table 3, mortgage-classification SGD experiments in Figure 1, and Higgs two-sample-testing experiments in Figure 2, with details in Appendix L.

after.justification: v2 retains all three original empirical studies, including revised attention benchmark values in Table 3 and the experiments documented in Appendix L.

M1.justification: The proposed thinning, attention, SGD-reordering, and testing procedures are retained. Algorithm 12 becomes Algorithm H.1 and expresses the same greedy MMD-minimizing replacements using an output copy and empirical-distribution notation; this does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate attention approximation on ImageNet 2012, logistic regression on Home Mortgage Disclosure Act data, and deep-kernel two-sample testing on Higgs data. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains exact attention, Performer, Reformer, ScatterBrain, and KDEformer. Figures 1–2 retain the same SGD and testing comparators. The added FlashAttention-2 citation does not represent an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix L.1 revises the attention experiment's reported software environment from PyTorch 2.4.1 to 2.6.0. The validation data, model and layer configurations, batch sizes, and timing procedure remain unchanged. This documents a setting revision without establishing which measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: The convergence trajectories in Figure 1 and time-power sweeps in Figure 2 are unchanged. Neither the main text nor the appendices add or remove ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five seeds for Table 3 accuracy and Figure 1, 50 batches for attention timing, and 1000 independent trials for Figure 2, with the same standard-deviation or standard-error reporting. Changed uncertainty values in Table 3 are result updates.

E6.justification: Table 3 updates several results: Performer accuracy changes from 80.53 ± 0.38% to 80.78 ± 0.17%, and ScatterBrain overtakes KDEformer as their accuracies change from 82.01/82.04% to 82.05/82.03%. Timings also change slightly. Thinformer's 82.17 ± 0.04% accuracy and Figures 1–2 remain unchanged. The revised software environment precludes interpreting these updates as identical-setting method improvements.

T1.justification: Section 6 adds that the existing MMD separation rate is minimax optimal for translation-invariant kernels, citing Kim and Schrab (2023, Theorem 8), beyond v1's statement of optimality among MMD tests. The paper's own theorem statements, assumptions, bounds, and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: general low-rank thinning guarantees and their applications to attention, SGD reordering, and efficient distribution testing. Neither the revised benchmark values nor the added background citations redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of low-rank adaptivity and the three empirical studies remain unchanged, as do the stated applicability conditions. The Impact Statement's added references to energy costs and training, inference, and evaluation elaborate the existing resource-saving rationale without adding a substantive limitation or mechanism.

D1.justification: Appendix L.1 updates the reported PyTorch dependency from 2.4.1 to 2.6.0. Hardware specifications, timing instructions, Table L.1 hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained, making this a localized reproducibility-information revision.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dao (2024) on FlashAttention-2 and Kim and Schrab (2023) on permutation tests. These extend the discussion of compatible attention implementations and testing optimality, while the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds an appendix contents list, adopts appendix-specific algorithm numbering, and makes localized edits to Section 4.2, Appendix H, and the Impact Statement. Remark 3 is incorporated into prose, and KH-REFINE pseudocode is reformulated. The overall narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The new appendix contents list causes localized reflow, Table 3 exchanges the KDEformer and ScatterBrain row positions, and the KH-REFINE algorithm block is reformatted. Figures 1–2 and the remaining table structures are retained; numerical updates are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: The appendix contents list and appendix-specific algorithm labels make the extensive supporting material easier to navigate, while the added citations improve contextual support. These are modest usability and exposition gains. The main guarantees and empirical coverage remain stable, and the revised Table 3 values under an updated reported software environment do not establish stronger method performance.
